title: Round Table
statement: Players sit around a round table, listed clockwise starting anywhere. For each player, return the score of the first player clockwise after them with a strictly higher score, going around the table if needed, or −1 if nobody has a higher score.

answerKey.pattern: Monotonic stack over the array twice
keyPoints: Walk indexes 0 to 2n − 1, using i % n
Use a decreasing stack of indexes waiting for a higher score
Only push indexes during the first lap
acceptableSlowerApproaches: For each player, walk around the table: O(n²)

hints: The answer can come from before the player in the list. How can a single pass look "around the corner"?
Walk the list twice: the second lap lets earlier players answer later ones.
Use i % n; push indexes only in the first lap, and pop answers in both laps.
